summary: Feed s133_double is degraded: 100% of packets are untagged so required VLANs 10 and 20 are missing, and IDS port is severely overloaded (2.89 Gbps burst vs 1 Gbps port, 289% capacity). Both reduce IDS detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or TAP/SPAN aggregation is stripping 802.1Q tags - 100% of packets arrive untagged so VLANs 10 and 20 are invisible. Typically caused by broker egress set to strip/untag or access mode instead of trunk/passthrough.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot identify or filter traffic by VLAN 10/20, loses segmentation visibility and misses VLAN-dependent detections and policy violations for those segments.

recommended_fix.why: Restore 802.1Q headers end-to-end so IDS receives correct VLAN 10/20 tags needed for VLAN-aware detection and correlation.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding bursty aggregate traffic peaking at 2.89 Gbps in 1ms intervals to a single 1 Gbps IDS port without load balancing or filtering, over-subscribing the port by 289% across 3 intervals.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS ingress buffers overflow and drops packets indiscriminately, causing missed signatures, broken TCP reassembly and incomplete payload inspection despite needing full payload and both directions.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 3x1 Gbps IDS ports (or add filtering/slicing) with 5-tuple hashing to keep per-port utilization below 80% and prevent drops while preserving both directions and full payload.
